prompt: I tested measurement invariance for my 9-item depression scale across two clinical groups. Configural and metric invariance both held. But when I imposed scalar invariance (equal intercepts), model fit got significantly worse — ΔCFI = -.024 and Δχ² was significant. I looked at the modification indices and two items have large intercept discrepancies across groups. Can I still compare mean depression levels between groups, and if so, how?
trap: The base model may say scalar invariance failed so group comparisons cannot be made, OR it may uncritically accept partial invariance without explaining the conditions. The correct answer explains partial scalar invariance as a defensible fallback when only a minority of items drive failure, names the threshold (~20% freed at most), and walks through the procedure.
assertions: Does NOT simply say scalar invariance failed so group mean comparison is impossible
Explains partial scalar invariance as a legitimate fallback when only a subset of items fail scalar constraints
States or implies a threshold for acceptable partial invariance — releasing ~20% of intercepts (here 2 of 9 = 22%) is at the edge; 1-2 items is more defensible
Explains that the non-invariant items must be freed AND that at least 2 intercepts per factor must remain constrained for identification
Requires substantive justification for why those specific items have different intercepts across groups — not just MI-based releasing
States that mean comparison with partial scalar invariance is defensible if conditions are met, but should be explicitly reported as partial rather than full invariance
